identity.standaloneProfile: signed-permit client bootstrap bound to appId=generator; no client role claim authorizes a future protected server operation
identity.schoolProfile: server-session enforcement is prepared in deployment configuration but remains deferred until an approved school runtime exists
identity.rule: Application identity, role and ownership claims from browser-controlled state are never sufficient evidence for a future server-side protected operation.

requestApiAi.controls: GHRAB AI Core operation registry, bounded request sizes and retries, explicit model profiles, teacher-opt-in url_context only on allowlisted operations, strict post-parse validation, no autonomous local tool loop or application side-effect executor.

egress.standalone: direct-gemini only, explicitly selected by the standalone runtime profile, without automatic fallback; real D3 student data is not approved for external AI egress by this local migration stage.
egress.school: school-gateway is the only school profile AI transport; local provider keys are forbidden and same-origin gateway enforcement remains server-phase deferred
egress.crossApp: Generator receives no generic cross-application network or administrative capability; Studio interaction is limited to signed access/bootstrap and release notification contracts.

files.currentBoundary: Teacher-controlled source text, images, documents, URLs and assignment JSON imports remain lower-trust inputs and pass existing type, size, checksum, parsing and sanitization controls before application or AI use.
files.serverBoundary: Server-side upload quarantine or document processing is not claimed; it remains deferred with the school-server phase.

dataLifecycle.classification: D3 school assessment data: teacher materials may coexist locally with student identifiers, answers and results; pseudonymization is not treated as anonymization.
dataLifecycle.storage: Namespaced localStorage/sessionStorage plus static PWA CacheStorage under public/config/data-manifest.json and suite-session cleanup rules.
dataLifecycle.retention: The current standalone profile retains client data until explicit end-work or browser site-data clearing; school-server retention is not active and must be re-verified when connected.
dataLifecycle.deletion: generatorEndWork and suite-session cleanup remove Generator-owned content and credentials with explicit reservations for security tombstones and non-owned shared state.

release.promotion: candidate -> cumulative QA/GARP gates -> certified pull request -> protected main -> exact release identity -> verified Pages deployment -> app-updated notification
release.publicAssurance: GitHub Pages remains a transitional public deployment; school-server SHIELD-LIVE and RI-LIVE are not claimed.
release.rollback: Existing release-integrity identity, Safe Promotion ancestry checks and prior releasable versions remain the rollback baseline.

inventory.changeRule: A new AI operation, provider tool, egress mode, import class, privileged browser capability, storage authority or release authority requires inventory update and matching tests before admission.

securityHealth.localCi: GARP 2.7 contract, G-02 policy admission, architecture-integrity, mutation, auto-patch, legacy GARP 2.5.1/N5 and existing P5/release controls remain active without the school server.
securityHealth.live: NOT_TESTED for school runtime until approved target infrastructure supplies trusted runtime evidence.
securityHealth.failureMode: Harness errors, empty scope, stale or mismatched evidence, missing required controls and unresolved critical imports never become PASS.

incident.current: Existing bounded error reporting, release evidence, fail-closed access behavior and Safe Promotion are retained; diagnostic content remains minimized and controlled.
incident.future: Central watchdog, server monitoring and infrastructure containment are deferred and require separate approval before activation.

recovery.current: Safe Promotion, exact release identity, deterministic build inputs, prior release history, local data cleanup and existing release-integrity tooling remain the recovery baseline.
recovery.future: Server restore, trust-root custody and live recovery drills remain NOT_TESTED until the school runtime is approved.
